tier_reason: First-party README bar chart (res/benchmark.png) of echo-server QPS vs libmill, golang and libco; benchmark sources are in the repo's benchmark/ directory but no CPU, OS, compiler or flags are given, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Bar chart only (values read from res/benchmark.png, approximate): at 100 concurrency libfiber ~232k QPS vs libmill ~201k, golang ~155k, libco ~147k; at 200 ~214k vs libco ~136k; at 500 ~196k vs libco ~128k; at 1000 ~178k vs libmill ~132k, golang ~123k, libco ~106k (about 1.6-1.7x vs libco, derived from page data)
corrections.caveats: First-party chart only; the page gives no CPU, OS, compiler or flags and no numeric table. Benchmark sources for libco and libmill are in the repo benchmark directory, golang sample and client live in acl-dev repos. Measures network echo IOPS, not raw context switch cost. libfiber is extracted from acl-dev/acl lib_fiber; the tboox benchbox switch page lists it as libfiber(acl), where it is slower than boost and tbox for raw switches.

notes: Chart values in the record match the image I downloaded. LGPL-3.0, 817 stars, last commit 2026-01-04 confirmed on github.com.

tier_reason: Third-party gist by the libcopp author (2019-09-29) with a table covering libgo, libco and linux ucontext; flags given (g++ -O2 -g -DNDEBUG) but no compiler version or CPU model and no well-known suite status, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Gist table (2019-09-29), libgo (current version) vs libco (static stack pool) vs linux ucontext: 1-coroutine switch 30 ns vs 84 ns vs 439 ns; 30000-coroutine switch 150 ns vs 450 ns vs 890 ns. The 1000-coroutine switch cell for libgo reads '32 us' on the page (likely a typo for ns; libco 168 ns, ucontext 505 ns). Creation is slower for libgo (8.3 us vs libco 3.9 us at 1000). C++20 stackless coroutines are faster than all stackful rows.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: g++ -O2 -g -DNDEBUG -ggdb -Wall -Werror -fPIC (per gist); compiler version not stated
corrections.caveats: Gist written by a competing library author (libcopp); CPU not stated, compiler version not stated. The table's libgo 1000-coroutine switch cell reads '32 us', probably a typo for ns. libgo uses 2 MB stacks vs 64 KB for libco/libcopp; a separate row for 2018 libgo built on boost is much slower (197 ns single switch). Gist comments ask for more libraries (librf, boost::fiber) and memory metrics; they do not dispute the libgo numbers. libgo's own README compares only against Go (2018 MacBook i5, graphs only). Boost.Context was not a column. Last commit 2023-03-10, over 3 years old.

notes: Numbers match the gist except the 1000-coroutine libgo cell, which the page prints as 32 us. Last commit 2023-03-10 is more than 3 years before today, so abandoned rather than stale. MIT and 3.3k stars confirmed.

tier_reason: Third-party shootout by the competing tbox author in VMs and on macOS with no compiler, flags or CPU model; libmill itself publishes no numbers, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: benchbox switch test, 2 coroutines: LinuxMint x86_64 VM libmill 145 ms vs boost 199 ms vs libco 687 ms (derived from page data: about 1.4x vs boost, 4.7x vs libco); macOS x86_64 libmill 525 ms vs boost 728 ms (libco not run); ArchLinux i386 VM libmill 689 ms vs boost 485 ms vs libco 774 ms (slower than boost). 1000 coroutines: libmill slower than boost on LinuxMint (1014 vs 894 ms) and ArchLinux (2031 vs 1021 ms), faster on macOS (1405 vs 1949 ms); faster than libco on both Linux runs (1014 vs 2288 ms, 2031 vs 3328 ms). tbox is fastest in every row.
corrections.hardware: macOS x86_64, ArchLinux i386 in VirtualBox, LinuxMint x86_64 in VirtualBox; CPU model not stated
corrections.caveats: Results against boost are mixed: win in 2-coroutine runs on LinuxMint and macOS, loss on ArchLinux i386 and at 1000 coroutines on both Linux VMs; consistently faster than libco. tbox beats it in every row. Benchmark run by the tbox author, no flags or CPU model. Repo claims no performance numbers itself. Last commit 2021-02-09.

notes: LinuxMint numbers in the record are correct, but the other two platforms on the same page show mixed results against boost; claim rewritten to cover all rows. Last commit 2021-02-09 from github.com commits page.
